props.gloss_en: the mishna: [the first shearing applies] but not with consecrated animals
why not with consecrated animals? the verse says 'your flock' -- and not a consecrated flock
[for altar sanctities indeed no verse is needed;] here we deal with sanctities for Temple maintenance
R' Elazar: sanctities for Temple maintenance are forbidden in shearing and in work
here it is one who consecrates his animal to Temple maintenance except for its shearings -- one might say: let him shear and give; the verse says 'your flock', not a flock of hekdesh
[an altar animal consecrated] 'except for shearing and weakening' -- even so the sanctity spreads through all of it
R' Yose: with consecrated animals, one who says 'the leg of this one is a burnt offering' -- all of it is a burnt offering
R' Meir: it is not all a burnt offering
even for R' Meir: that is where he consecrated something on which life does not depend; but if he consecrated something on which life depends, it [all] is consecrated
Rava: [it is] where he consecrates the shearing itself -- one might say: let him shear, redeem and give
Rava: the verse says 'the first shearing of your flock you shall give him' -- one lacking only shearing and giving; excluded is this one, lacking shearing, redemption and giving
the baraita: an animal of partners is obligated in the first shearing
and R' Ilai exempts [partners from the first shearing]
R' Ilai's reason: the verse says 'your flock' -- and not one of a partnership
and the Rabbis: [tzonkha] excludes partnership with a gentile
R' Ilai derives [gentile partnership's exemption] from the start of the verse, 'the first of your grain' -- and not a partnership with a gentile
a Jew and a gentile who bought a field in partnership -- untithed and non-sacred produce are mixed in one another; the words of Rebbi
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel: the Jew's [portion] is obligated and the gentile's is exempt
they disagree only in that one master holds there is retroactive clarification and one holds there is not
but partnership with a gentile -- all agree it is obligated [in teruma]
for R' Ilai, both [partnership with a Jew and with a gentile] are derived from 'your flock'
partnership with a gentile -- what is the reason? that it is not exclusively his; with a Jew too it is not exclusively his
and the Rabbis? a gentile is not subject to obligation; a Jew is subject to obligation
Rava: R' Ilai concedes [partners are obligated] in teruma: though 'your grain' is written (yours, not partnership), the Merciful One wrote 'your [pl.] terumot'
then why 'your grain'? to exclude partnership with a gentile
challa: though 'reishit' is written (one could learn reishit/reishit from the first shearing), the Merciful One wrote 'your [pl.] dough'
why 'your dough'? [to teach the measure:] as much as your dough
pe'a: though 'your field' is written, the Merciful One wrote 'and when you [pl.] reap the harvest of your land'
then why 'your field'? to exclude partnership with a gentile
bechora: though 'in your herd and your flock' is written, the Merciful One wrote 'the firstborn of your [pl.] herd and flock'
then why 'your herd and your flock'? to exclude partnership with a gentile
mezuza: though 'your house' is written, the Merciful One wrote 'that your [pl.] days may be multiplied, and the days of your children'
Rabba: [beitekha teaches] by way of your entry -- from the right
ma'aser: though 'the tithe of your grain' is written, the Merciful One wrote 'your [pl.] tithes'
then what does 'the tithe of your grain' come for? to exclude partnership with a gentile
the gifts: though 'and he shall give' is written (one could learn netina/netina from the first shearing), the Merciful One wrote 'from those [pl.] who slaughter the slaughter'
[then 'those who slaughter' is] for Rava's teaching: the claim [for the gifts] is against the butcher
bikkurim: though 'your land' is written, the Merciful One wrote 'the first fruits of all that is in their land'
then why 'your land'? to exclude outside the Land
tzitzit: though 'your covering' is written, the Merciful One wrote 'on the corners of their garments throughout their generations'
Rav Yehuda: a borrowed cloak is exempt from tzitzit for all thirty days
ma'akeh: though 'for your roof' is written, the Merciful One wrote 'if any man fall from it'
then what does 'your roof' come for? to exclude synagogues and study halls
these rules [Rava's list of R' Ilai's concessions] do not hold
the baraita: an animal of partners is obligated in the firstborn law
and R' Ilai exempts it [from the firstborn law]
R' Ilai's reason: it is written 'your herd and your flock'
the baraita: an animal of partners is obligated in the gifts
and R' Ilai exempts [partners from the gifts]
rather, conclude from it: in teruma too he [R' Ilai] exempts [partners]
R' Ilai: the gifts apply only in the Land
and so R' Ilai would say: the first shearing applies only in the Land
R' Yose of Neharbil: yes -- [as with teruma, the gifts apply] in the Land and not outside it
[Abaye:] as teruma, not from new on behalf of old -- so the first shearing? [Rava:] yes
the baraita: he had two ewes, sheared and set aside, sheared and set aside, two or three years -- they do not combine
it follows: five [over the years] do combine
but it is taught: they do not combine
a Jew who bought a field in Syria from a gentile: before [the produce] reached a third -- obligated
after it reached a third -- R' Akiva obligates the additional growth
and the Sages exempt
for teruma: what grew under obligation is obligated, what grew under exemption is exempt -- and for teruma, from where? as taught [in the Syria baraita]
[Abaye:] so the first shearing too: what grew under obligation is obligated, under exemption exempt -- and if you say so indeed [for R' Ilai]
the mishna: one who buys the shearing of a gentile's flock is exempt from the first shearing
it follows: [one who bought] his flock to shear is obligated
our mishna is not according to R' Ilai
the baraita: he had two kinds of figs, black and white, or two kinds of wheat -- one does not separate teruma or tithes from one on behalf of the other
Beit Shammai: one does not separate teruma [from one on the other]
Beit Hillel: one does separate teruma [from one on the other]
for teruma: not from one kind on behalf of another -- and for teruma, from where? as taught
[Abaye:] so the first shearing, not from one kind on behalf of another? [Rava:] yes
the mishna: if he had two kinds, grey and white, and sold him the grey but not the white, the males but not the females -- this one gives for himself and that one gives for himself
rather, [the mishna] teaches us good advice -- here too good advice: that he give them from both
[Abaye:] as teruma requires a first portion whose remainder is recognisable, so the first shearing? [Rava:] yes
the mishna: one who says 'all my threshing floor is teruma' or 'all my dough is challa' has said nothing
it follows: 'all my shearings are reishit' -- his words stand
and another [baraita] teaches: ['all my shearings are reishit'] -- he has said nothing
nowadays the world's practice follows these three elders: R' Ilai on the first shearing
...and R' Yehuda ben Beteira on words of Torah
R' Yehuda ben Beteira: words of Torah do not receive impurity
...and R' Yoshiya on kilayim
R' Yoshiya: one is never liable until he sows wheat, barley and a grape pit in one throw of the hand
